Inclusion-heavy allocation (30/10/10) at the default 0.6-1.4 scale was the round's best (0.5746, inclusion 0.329). Next: keep default scale for scratches, try small scale ONLY for inclusion/patches, and probe whether the small scratches cost from inclusion-heavy allocation can be recovered (e.g. slightly more scratches or any_class backgrounds).

candidates.hypothesis: Small-paste-scale hypothesis: misses concentrate in the low size tertile, so shrinking pastes to the missed size range (inclusion 0.3-0.7x, patches/scratches 0.4-0.8x) should raise small-instance recall. Confirmed if mAP50 beats the balanced/default control, especially inclusion AP50 and low-tertile recall, without a precision collapse.

Allocation hypothesis: inclusion is the starved, worst class (10 real images, AP50 0.179, 148 missed), so at the default scale range, shifting 30 of 50 images to inclusion should lift inclusion AP50 most. Confirmed if inclusion AP50 rises substantially and overall mAP50 beats the balanced control; if not, allocation balance matters less than scale.

Combination hypothesis: if small scale and inclusion-heavy allocation both help, their combination should be the round's best (additive effects). Confirmed if it has the highest mAP50; if it underperforms A or B, the two factors interact negatively and I should not stack them in later rounds.

lesson: Default-scale inclusion (0.6-1.4) at 30/10/10 is the best recipe: it extended mAP50 to 0.6614 with the best scratches (0.757) and competitive inclusion (0.490), beating the small-inclusion variant. Pushing inclusion to 40 (candidate 2) backfired — inclusion AP50 fell to 0.410 and mAP50 dropped, so 30 is the sweet spot and 5/5 starvation of the other classes is not worth it. Small patches (candidate 3) recovered patches (0.800) but cost inclusion and scratches, a net loss; the default recipe is the final bet.

candidates.hypothesis: Default-scale inclusion repeat: the Round-2 control recipe (default 0.6-1.4 inclusion, 30/10/10) had the highest mAP50 (0.6334) and best patches (0.780); the small-inclusion gain in inclusion AP50 (+0.036) was offset by the patches cost (-0.085). Repeating the default recipe in round 3 on the cumulative set should hold or extend the mAP50 lead. Confirmed if mAP50 >= 0.6334 with patches AP50 >= 0.75 and inclusion AP50 >= 0.45.

Inclusion-cap push: inclusion is still the worst class (AP50 0.493, low-tertile recall 0.288, 112 missed at ~33px) and small-scale 0.3-0.7 pastes are the proven lever for it; inclusion AP50 rose with every +30 small inclusions (0.329 -> 0.457 -> 0.493), so spending more of the 45 headroom (40 vs 30) should lift inclusion further, and the small reduction of patches/scratches to 5 each is tolerable since both sit near 0.70. Confirmed if inclusion AP50 > 0.50 and mAP50 beats the small-inclusion 30/10/10 control; if it loses, 30 is the sweet spot and allocation balance matters more than I thought.

Small-patches recovery: under small inclusion, patches AP50 dropped to 0.695 (vs 0.780 with default inclusion) because small inclusion pastes resemble small patches; missed patches are small (median 54.6px, low-tertile recall 0.578, n=90) and Round 1 showed 0.4-0.8x patches were not harmful to patches (0.785 vs 0.765 control). Adding small patches should sharpen the patch/inclusion boundary and recover the dip while keeping the inclusion gain. Confirmed if patches AP50 > 0.74, inclusion AP50 > 0.48, and mAP50 > 0.6334; if patches stay < 0.72, small patches do not fix the interaction and the default recipe (A) is the safer final bet.
